source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check TPM in BIOS/OS

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- TPM detection: the agent reads the OS TPM detection sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls -l /dev/tpm0 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i 'tpm' | grep -i 'found\|2.0'; cat /sys/class/tpm/tpm0/tpm_version_major 2>&1" but the BIOS-side TPM presence is a Setup screen the user/KVM reads.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return /dev/tpm0 + tpm_version_major + the "found/2.0 TPM" dmesg lines; BIOS TPM setting read by user/KVM.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: BIOS-side detection check needs a person/KVM; agent provides the OS-equivalent read.

original_test_intent: Confirm the same expected TPM is present and correctly reported in both BIOS/UEFI and the operating system without changing TPM state.
original_method: A qualified operator or approved KVM session records the BIOS TPM page; the agent collects read-only OS device, sysfs, kernel and optional approved tpm2 capability data, then correlates version/manufacturer/state across interfaces.
manual_activity: The source requires BIOS-side confirmation through a Pre-OS setup screen. OS evidence is automatable but cannot replace that required human/KVM observation, so the core acceptance is manual.
required_inputs: Expected TPM type/generation, manufacturer and enabled/present state
Exact BIOS/UEFI path and firmware version
Approved KVM/console observer and evidence policy
OS/kernel driver and optional tpm2-tools version
Final unchanged state and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Keep all operations read-only; never clear, re-own, provision, enable/disable or generate keys.
Do not assume `/dev/tpm0`; enumerate all relevant TPM device/sysfs nodes.
Protect security evidence and stop on BIOS/OS disagreement or unexpected ownership/state.
Retain existing kernel/SEL evidence and do not remediate automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Enumerate OS TPM device/resource-manager nodes, sysfs identity and kernel messages with approved read-only tools.
Correlate OS properties with operator/KVM BIOS evidence and flag discrepancies.
Do not interact with BIOS, change TPM state or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Supply expected TPM and BIOS path.
Observe and record the BIOS/UEFI TPM view.
Review cross-interface evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The reads are useful on compatible Linux systems, but fixed device/version paths and grep patterns are not portable or sufficient alone.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain BIOS observation and use platform-tolerant read-only enumeration; use the linked self-test script only after review and do not let self-test replace detection scope.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both BIOS and OS views, linked script field and both ten-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN DUAL-INTERFACE DETECTION WITH PLATFORM-TOLERANT OS INVENTORY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record BIOS evidence separately, enumerate `/dev/tpm*` and `/sys/class/tpm/`, capture kernel identity and use approved read-only tpm2 fixed properties where supported, correlating manufacturer/version/state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Target BIOS/UEFI and OS TPM stack.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, TPM firmware, OS/kernel and tpm2-tools/script versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner platform TPM/BIOS specification and reviewed repository script revision.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity correlation and removes fixed-path assumptions without changing interfaces.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; BIOS and OS remain independently evidenced.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected identity/state, BIOS path and OS tool support.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS device presence alone does not prove the firmware view or policy state.

project_override_considerations: A project may select approved read-only OS tools, but cannot omit the BIOS view while claiming this case. Any TPM self-test or provisioning is separate coverage.
expected_evidence: Platform/BIOS/TPM identity, expected state, tool versions and authorization
OS device/sysfs/kernel and approved capability output correlated to BIOS
No-state-change confirmation, security/host health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion consistently require BIOS and OS detection; the lack of exact expected state is a readiness input.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Expected TPM data and KVM access can be provided; the case is MANUAL ONLY due to BIOS observation, not blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Change PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY under V3.1 because BIOS visual acceptance is core; keep its OS evidence only as support.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its cross-interface and read-only safeguards while changing classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates BIOS observation, OS tool results and final engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Avoids fixed-path false negatives and prevents OS detection from being reported as proof of the required BIOS view.
independent_technical_reasoning: The test explicitly names two independent interfaces. OS discovery can be automated, but required BIOS visual evidence remains a human Pre-OS observation; neither interface can substitute for the other.
